This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game studio. Then it explains one idea. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. Every question on this page
has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary media-package production-brief production-role production-schedule handoff naming-convention production-log quality-review quality-criterion storyboard promo-clip credits-file >}}

## 14.1 The brief and the package

- A **production brief** says what to make, for whom, the format and
  length, and the deadline.
- The **media package** has five parts: a **storyboard** (6 panels), a
  **sound set** (3 effects and a loop), a **promo clip** (30 s, 16:9), a
  **credits file** and a **quality review**.
- Salma's brief: players on phones and PCs; a dark, tense night; PNG, 48
  kHz WAV, MP4 16:9 with peaks at −1 dB or lower; the end of session 2.

![The media package.](images/package.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Read the brief before you produce anything.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Write the brief"}
Write the brief of your package in five lines: what, for whom, mood,
formats, deadline.

::: {.check}
A good brief looks like: "What: a storyboard, a sound set, a 30 s promo
and a credits file for Storm Night. For whom: players on phones and PCs.
Mood: dark, rainy, tense. Formats: PNG, 48 kHz WAV, MP4 16:9. Deadline:
the end of session 2." Check: five lines, real formats, a real deadline.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · The parts of the package"}
Which part of the package is it?

::: {.match extra="the production log|the schedule"}
6 panels with a shot list
:   the storyboard

    Why: The storyboard plans the shots of the promo.

3 sound effects and a music loop
:   the sound set

    Why: The sound set holds the sounds of the package.

30 s, 16:9, with music
:   the promo clip

    Why: The promo clip is the video of the package.

a TASL line for every asset
:   the credits file

    Why: The credits file names the source and the licence of each asset.
:::
:::

## 14.2 Roles, schedule and handoffs

- Four roles: **producer**, **storyboard artist**, **sound designer**,
  **video editor**.
- A **schedule** puts the tasks in order.
- A **handoff** passes finished work to the next role.
- The storyboard comes before the capture, the music loop before the cut,
  the credits before the export.

![Four roles.](images/roles.png){width=94%}

![The handoffs.](images/pipeline.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/production-planner.html" poster="sims/production-planner.png" title="Production Planner: two sessions, eight tasks" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A task that needs another task's result waits for the handoff.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Plan the sessions"}
Remove all conflicts in **Production Planner**. Then write your own
schedule: role, task, slot.

::: {.check}
A plan without conflicts: 1a storyboard, sound effects, music loop; 1b
capture, credits file; 2a cut and titles; 2b mix and export, then the
quality review. In your schedule, every task comes after the tasks it
needs.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Handoffs"}
Use Production Planner. Choose the answer.

::: {.match extra="the brief|the sound effects"}
The editor wants to capture gameplay. What must be finished first?
:   the storyboard and shot list

    Why: The editor must know which shots to capture.

The editor wants to cut the promo on the music. What must be finished first?
:   the capture and the music loop

    Why: The cut needs the shots and the music.

The credits file is not ready. Which task must wait?
:   the mix and export

    Why: The package goes out only with complete credits.

Which task comes last of all?
:   the quality review

    Why: The review checks the finished package.
:::
:::

## 14.3 Files, names and the production log

- One shared folder with numbered subfolders.
- A **naming convention:** `level_type_name_version`, no spaces.
- **One owner per file**, and a dated **production log**.

![One folder, one naming rule.](images/naming.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Nothing stays only on one laptop: everything goes into the shared folder.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Folder and log"}
Create the folder structure. Write three lines of your production log.

::: {.check}
Six subfolders: 01_brief, 02_storyboard, 03_audio, 04_video, 05_credits,
06_review. A good log line: "10:15, Sara, panels 1–6 v01, the lightning
shot moves to panel 2": a time, a name, a file version, a decision.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Files"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="final_final2.wav|Storm Thunder NEW.wav"}
What is a good name for version 2 of a rain sound of the level "storm"?
:   storm_sfx_rain_v02.wav

    Why: Level, type, name and version, with no spaces.

Who saves the promo edit?
:   the video editor only

    Why: One owner per file, so no changes are lost.

What does a line of the production log have?
:   the date, who, what, a decision

    Why: The log is a dated record of the work and the decisions.

Where does every asset belong?
:   in the shared folder

    Why: If one person is absent, the package is still complete.
:::
:::

## 14.4 The quality review: the brief and five criteria

- **Step 1, the brief:** brief value, measured value, **pass** or **fail**.
- **Step 2, the quality:** five **criteria**, each scored from 1 to 4 with
  **evidence**: fits the gameplay, consistent, technical, clear, rights
  cleared.
- Fix the fails first; the owner of each file makes its fix. Then check
  again.

![Five quality criteria with their evidence.](images/quality-criteria.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/package-checker.html" poster="sims/package-checker.png" title="Package Checker: does it meet the brief?" height="700" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Length, shape and peaks are numbers: measure them. Score the evidence, not
the effort.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Check version 1"}
Mark and fix version 1 in **Package Checker**. Then score your own package
on the five criteria, with evidence.

::: {.check}
Pass: the storyboard and the music loop. Fail: the length (41 s), the
shape (9:16), the peak (0 dB), the credits (two sounds missing). Fixes:
cut the intro shot, export in 16:9, lower the master, add two TASL lines.
Your scores: five numbers from 1 to 4, each with evidence.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The review"}
Use Package Checker. Choose the answer.

::: {.match extra="make it louder|add more shots"}
The promo is 41 s, and the brief says 30 s. What is the fix?
:   cut the slow intro shot

    Why: The intro adds the extra time, and the best shots stay.

The promo is 9:16, and the brief says 16:9. What is the fix?
:   export again with the 16:9 preset

    Why: The shape is a setting of the export.

The loudest peak is 0 dB. What is the fix?
:   lower the master and export again

    Why: The brief asks for peaks at −1 dB or lower.

The music is bright and happy, but the brief is dark and tense. Which criterion is weak?
:   consistent

    Why: Consistent means one art style and one sound mood.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Workshop Day {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Six problems in the Storm Night workshop: a **late storyboard**, files
called **"final"**, **two editors** in one project, a **clicking loop**, a
promo in **9:16**, and a student **alone**.

{{< sim file="sims/workshop-day.html" poster="sims/workshop-day.png" title="Workshop Day: six production problems" kind="game" height="500" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · The problems"}
Six problems: a late storyboard, files called "final", two editors in one
project, a clicking loop, a promo in 9:16, a student alone. Choose what to
do.

::: {.match extra="skip the storyboard|delete all files"}
The storyboard is not ready for the capture.
:   finish the storyboard and shot list first

    Why: They are the handoff before the capture.

The folder has "final.wav" and "final2.wav".
:   use the naming rule with versions

    Why: storm_music_loop_v03.wav shows which file is the newest.

Two members edit the same promo project and lose changes.
:   one owner per file; the others send notes

    Why: Only the owner saves the file.

The music loop clicks when it starts again.
:   cut at a loop point with tiny fades

    Why: A seamless loop ends where a bar ends, with no click (Lecture 8).

A student works alone.
:   take each role in turn and keep a log

    Why: The same package is made role by role, with a dated log.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- One brief leads to one media package: storyboard, sound set, promo,
  credits file, quality review.
- Roles and a schedule with handoffs keep the work in order.
- One folder, one naming rule, one owner per file and a production log
  keep the files safe.
- The quality review checks the brief (pass or fail) and five criteria
  with evidence.
- Fix the fails first, then check again.
